Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being reminded of the event by others
Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

vignette: Carlos, a 26-year-old Latin American man, had endured torture in his home country before fleeing to the United States. Now divorced and working as a maid, Carlos struggles daily with the intrusive memories that linger from his traumatic past. The trauma has profoundly shaped his life and responses to everyday situations. One particularly haunting trigger for Carlos is seeing cars similar to those used by the torturers during his ordeal. Every time he spots such vehicles while driving or walking around his neighborhood, he experiences a wave of anxiety and distress. These triggers are not just passive reminders; they actively drive him into avoidance behaviors that have become deeply ingrained over time. Carlos had come to believe that being reminded of the event by others would only intensify his pain and fear. As such, he avoids situations where people might bring up the past or inadvertently trigger memories through conversation. He also tends to avoid authority figures and anyone in uniform because they remind him of those who perpetrated violence against him. His smoking habit is one way Carlos copes with these triggers. Every time a reminder surfaces, whether from seeing a similar car on his route home or watching a news segment that touches on themes related to his experience, he reaches for a cigarette. He had come to believe that the numbing effect of nicotine helped to dull the emotional pain temporarily. The threat perception Carlos faces is palpable and relentless. He wakes up several times each night, convinced that danger lurks in the shadows, checking repeatedly if he is truly safe. Even a casual touch from someone can send him into an immediate state of alarm, his heart racing as though he were back at the hands of those who tortured him. His fear of strangers has intensified to the point where walking through public spaces leaves Carlos feeling vulnerable and threatened. This constant vigilance feeds into his avoidance behaviors, creating a vicious cycle that feels inescapable. The more he avoids reminders and authority figures, the more isolated and anxious he becomes, reinforcing the belief that these triggers are indeed dangerous. Carlos's occupation as a maid places him in varied environments where these triggers can easily be encountered. He often finds himself avoiding certain routes to work or skipping shifts altogether to avoid potential exposure. This pattern has led to conflicts with his supervisors, who notice the erratic schedule and declining performance. These occupational consequences have only heightened Carlos’s sense of instability and fear. Despite his efforts to manage the symptoms through avoidance and smoking, the triggers continue to intrude into his daily life. For instance, a recent news segment about human rights abuses in Latin America sent him spiraling back into severe anxiety for days. He had come to believe that any positive emotions were also dangerous because they could be shattered by an unexpected trigger. It was this growing sense of helplessness and the increasing impact on his work and life that finally drove Carlos to seek help. He was certain that he needed support to break free from these overwhelming fears, hoping to regain a semblance of normalcy and peace in his daily existence. What frightened him most was the possibility of never escaping the constant reminders and threats, leaving him perpetually trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance. Carlos’s current state is one of deep anxiety and isolation, but he remains hopeful that therapy can provide him with the tools to navigate these fears more effectively. He looks forward to finding ways to mitigate his triggers and reduce the overwhelming sense of threat that has dominated his life since fleeing torture.
